comments.author: @giannisolga5191
comments.text: I worked in Saudi Arabia 1978-1980. The town where I worked was 50,000 population. It is now 1,340,000.  The cliffs I climbed with sheer drops of 1,000 meters now have a telepherique! We slept undisturbed in tents on Sudah, now overrun with tourists. What we had all too ourselves has now been changed beyond recognition. It is an area receiving large numbers of tourists, where none existed in our time. And all of this made possible by desalination plants on the Red Sea. The pristine coral reefs that Jacques Cousteau called the finest in the world will be changed by the huge amounts of concentrated brine that the desalination plants are returning to the sea. I do not begrudge the land for its development, but I am glad that I was there when it was still like its ancient self. With bedouin markets where cubes of packed dates half a meter thick, frankincense and myrrh were sold.
